Shape analysis has been identified as a potential supplement to conventional lesion characterization in cases of suspected internal carotid artery thrombus. Five quantitative shape descriptors of carotid FFT (Carotid Fibre Tree) have been discovered, which may help differentiate between free-floating internal carotid artery thrombus and atherosclerotic plaque.

The presence of a carotid thrombus is typically diagnosed using Computed Tomography Angiography (CTA) for stroke or transient ischemic attack. However, some patients may present with features that resemble atherosclerotic plaque on CTA imaging, potentially masking the true nature of their condition.

Shape analysis, which involves analyzing the unique patterns and features of carotid artery morphology, can provide valuable additional information in these cases. By examining the quantitative shape descriptors of the carotid FFT, healthcare providers may be able to identify differences between a thrombus and an atherosclerotic plaque that are not visible on traditional CTA imaging.

While shape analysis is still a developing field, the current evidence suggests that it has potential as a supplementary tool in diagnosing and differentiating between these two conditions. Further research is needed to fully explore the utility of shape analysis in this context.
